declared.title: Lost in the mall again: a preregistered replication and extension of Loftus & Pickrell (1995)
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « Lost in the mall again: a preregistered replication and extension of Loftus and Pickrell » (2026-11-23)

population: adults (Ireland, per Andrews & Brewin 2024) interviewed twice about true childhood events and one fabricated event, from a relative's information

findings.text: A preregistered replication coded 35% of people as reporting a false memory of getting lost in a mall as a child (25% in the original study)

support.sentence: We replicated the findings of the original study, coding 35% of participants as reporting a false memory for getting lost in a mall in childhood (compared to 25% in the original study).

findings.text: Participants themselves also reported high rates of memories and beliefs for the made-up event

support.sentence: In an extension, we found that participants self-reported high rates of memories and beliefs for the fabricated event.

limits: a reanalysis of the same transcripts (Andrews & Brewin 2024) finds that few suggested details were recalled and that many reports may be real memories
one country, 123 people; getting lost is a mild childhood fright, not a harmless everyday event
a duplicate copy of this article was published by error and withdrawn (notice read, see acknowledged)

acknowledged.changes: notice of duplicate publication: a second copy (10.1080/09658211.2023.2198263) was withdrawn; this version of record and its results are unchanged
